verses.zh: 锡安哪，兴起！兴起！披上你的能力！圣城耶路撒冷啊，穿上你华美的衣服！因为从今以后，未受割礼、不洁净的必不再进入你中间。
verses.en: Wake up! Wake up!Clothe yourself with strength, O Zion!Put on your beautiful clothes,O Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] holy city.For uncircumcised and unclean paganswill no longer invade you.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
52:1-2 "Awake. . .clothe. . .shake. . .loose" This is a series of IMPERATIVES
(see Contextual Insights, B), like Isa. 51:9,17. Many compare this with the opposite condition of the
city of Babylon in Isa. 47:1ff.

Notice the conditional element involved in these IMPERATIVES. The
returnees must act to receive YHWH's deliverance.

52:1e "For the uncircumcised and the unclean

Will no longer come into you" In context this cannot refer to the exclusion
of the Gentiles from redemption, but that no heathen nation would again invade the Promised Land. This
may be the source of John's imagery in Rev. 21:27, as well as Peter's in 1 Pet. 1:4.

See full note at 51:22 related to conditional covenants.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷啊，要抖下尘土！起来坐在位上！锡安被掳的居民（原文是女子）哪，要解开你颈项的锁链！
verses.en: Shake off the dirt![NOTE:1] Get up, captive[NOTE:2] Jerusalem. Take off the iron chains around your neck,O captive daughter Zion.
notes: Heb “Shake yourself free from the dirt.”

The Hebrew text has שְּׂבִי (shevi), which some understand as a feminine singular imperative from יָשַׁב (yashav, “sit”). The LXX, Vulgate, Syriac, and the Targum support the MT reading (the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa does indirectly). Some interpret this to mean “take your throne”: The Lord exhorts Jerusalem to get up from the dirt and sit, probably with the idea of sitting in a place of honor (J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 2:361)(cf. NLT, NIV, TNIV, HCSB). However, the form likely needs to be emended to שְׁבִיָּה (sheviyyah, “captive”), which appears in the parallel line (cf. NASB, RSV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
52:2

NASB, NRSV, NJB, REB, NET
"captive"

NKJV, LXX, Peshitta
"sit down"

Vulgate, TEV, JPSOA
"sit [on your throne]"

The MT has "sit" (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal IMPERATIVE,
שבי, but later in the verse שביה (BDB 985), is
translated "captive." The UBS Text Project, p. 140, gives "sit" a B rating (some doubt). Israel is to rise
up and sit on her throne or in a place of prominence.

▣ "Loose" This is a place where the MT has a MASCULINE PLURAL form
of the Hithpael IMPERATIVE (i.e. "they were opening," BDB 834 I, KB 986, ), but the Masoretic
scholars suggested (qere) a FEMININE SINGULAR form (i.e. "loose yourselves," NASB).
They both would refer to a personified Jerusalem. The UBS Text Project, p. 140, gives the MT a C rating.

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：「你们是无价被卖的，也必无银被赎。
verses.en: For this is what the Lord says:“You were sold for nothing,and you will not be redeemed for money.”
verses.commentary:
52:3 "redeemed without money" This verse must be seen in light of Isa. 45:13. Cyrus II will
let all the captive exiles return freely. Cyrus II reversed the relocation policy of both the Assyrians and
Babylonians. He allowed all conquered peoples to return home and rebuild their national temples. This
was his way of restoring order to his empire and also he was superstitious and wanted all the returning
people groups to pray to their gods for him and his successors.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：起先我的百姓下到埃及，在那里寄居，又有亚述人无故欺压他们。
verses.en: For this is what the Sovereign Lord says:“In the beginning my people went to live temporarily in Egypt;Assyria oppressed them for no good reason.
verses.commentary:
52:4-5 Verse 5 is referring to Neo-Babylonian exile though Neo-Babylon is not mentioned by name. These
verses are looking at past oppression (i.e. Egypt and Assyria). Theologically Israel and Judah were exiled
because of their sin against YHWH (cf. Isa. 43:22-24; 50:1).

52:4 "Egypt. . .Assyrian" These were two of the covenant people's previous enemies before
that of Neo-Babylon (cf. Isa. 10:5ff).

verses.zh: 耶和华说：我的百姓既是无价被掳去，如今我在这里做甚么呢？耶和华说：辖制他们的人呼叫，我的名整天受亵渎。
verses.en: And now, what do we have here?”[NOTE:1] says the Lord.“Indeed my people have been carried away for nothing,those who rule over them taunt,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord, “and my name is constantly slandered[NOTE:3] all day long.
notes: Heb “and now what [following the marginal reading (Qere)] to me here?”

The verb appears to be a Hiphil form from the root יָלַל (yalal, “howl”), perhaps here in the sense of “mock.” Some emend the form to יְהוֹלָלוֹ (yeholalo) and understand a Polel form of the root הָלַל meaning here “mock, taunt.”
The verb is apparently a Hitpolal form (with assimilated tav, ת) from the root נָאַץ (naʾats), but GKC 151-52 §55.b explains it as a mixed form, combining Pual and Hitpolel readings.
verses.commentary:
52:5 There are several ways to view the Hebrew text related to the rulers ("those who rule,"
BDB 605, KB 647, Qal PARTICIPLE)

- the leaders of Jerusalem who "howl" or "wail" (BDB 410, KB 413, Hiphil IMPERFECT)
over the fall of Jerusalem

- the leaders of Neo-Babylon who "mock" (BDB 237 II, cf. Isa. 44:25) as Jerusalem falls

▣ "My name is continually blasphemed" This VERB (BDB 610, KB 658) is
a rare Hithpolel form (i.e. "be scorned"). God's name was linked to Israel's condition. God will act, not because of
Israel's goodness but because of His name (cf. Isa. 48:11; Ezek. 20:9,14,22,44; 36:19-20,22-23; Dan. 9:17-19;
Rom. 2:24).

verses.zh: 所以，我的百姓必知道我的名；到那日他们必知道说这话的就是我。看哪，是我！」
verses.en: For this reason my people will know my name;for this reason they will know[NOTE:1] at that time[NOTE:2] that I am the one who says,‘Here I am.’”
notes: The verb is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Heb “in that day” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
verses.commentary:
52:6 By YHWH's deliverance His people will know that He has reestablished the covenant. His
name will have meaning again!

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

▣ "in that day" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

▣

NASB, NJB, REB
"Here I am"

NKJV
"Behold, it it I"

NRSV
"Here am I"

JPSOA
"Am now at hand"

LXX
"I am here"

Peshitta
"It is I"

This phrase is usually a faith response from a human being who has
been addressed by God (i.e. Gen. 22:1,11; Exod. 3:4; Isa. 6:8). It would denote availability to
do God's will.

It is only in Isaiah that it is used of God and denotes His presence, power,
and ability to do what He promised (cf. Isa. 58:9; 65:1).

verses.zh: 那报佳音，传平安，报好信，传救恩的，对锡安说：你的　神作王了！这人的脚登山何等佳美！
verses.en: How delightful it is to see approaching over the mountains[NOTE:1] the feet of a messenger who announces peace,a messenger who brings good news, who announces deliverance,who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “How delightful on the mountains.”

Or “has become king.” When a new king was enthroned, his followers would give this shout. For other examples of this enthronement formula (Qal perfect third person masculine singular מָלַךְ [malakh], followed by the name of the king), see 2 Sam 15:10; 1 Kgs 1:11, 13, 18; 2 Kgs 9:13. The Lord is an eternal king, but here he is pictured as a victorious warrior who establishes his rule from Zion.
verses.commentary:
52:7-9 These verses are using the imagery of

- a governmental messenger bringing good news (cf. Isa. 52:7)

- the watchman (cf. Isa. 52:8) at the gate announcing it to the whole city

The city is Zion; the good news is that YHWH reigns again as King over His
restored people (i.e. in His temple).

52:7 The Hebrew VERB "bring good news" (BDB 142, KB 163, Piel
PARTICIPLE, twice, cf. Isa. 40:9; 41:27; 61:1-9) is alluded to in Rom. 10:15 for the "good news"
of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

- substitutionary atonement (cf. Isa. 52:13-53:12)

- presence of Immanuel (cf. Isa. 7:14)

- no distinction between Jew and Greek (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

▣ Notice the parallelism between the announced good news.

- peace (BDB 1022)

- happiness/good (BDB 373 I)

- salvation (BDB 447)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT, shalom)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT)

▣ "Your God reigns" This (BDB 573, KB 590, Qal PERFECT)
is the fulfillment of Isa. 24:23. It may reflect a well known Israeli liturgy (cf. Ps. 93:1; 96:10; 97:1; 99:1).

verses.zh: 听啊，你守望之人的声音，他们扬起声来，一同歌唱；因为耶和华归回锡安的时候，他们必亲眼看见。
verses.en: Listen,[NOTE:1] your watchmen shout;in unison they shout for joy,for they see with their very own eyes[NOTE:2] the Lord’s return to Zion.
notes: קוֹל (qol, “voice”) is used at the beginning of the verse as an interjection.
Heb “eye in eye”; KJV, ASV “eye to eye”; NAB “directly, before their eyes.”
verses.commentary:
52:8

NASB, TEV, NJB
"they will see with their own eyes"

NKJV, Peshitta
"they shall see eye to eye"

NRSV
"in plain sight they see"

JPSOA
"every eye shall behold"

NET Bible
"they will see with their very own eyes"

LXX
"eyes shall look at eyes"

The MT has "eye to eye." Leupold, in his commentary on Isaiah, makes a good point.

"The phrase 'eye to eye' has an utterly different meaning in English than in Hebrew. In
English it means something like agreeing completely in one's approach and outlook with another. In
Hebrew the meaning is 'close at hand,' something like being so near that you can see the whites of the
eye of the person approaching" (p. 219).

▣ "When the Lord restores Zion" See Daniel 9:24-27.

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷的荒场啊，要发起欢声，一同歌唱；因为耶和华安慰了他的百姓，救赎了耶路撒冷。
verses.en: In unison give a joyful shout,O ruins of Jerusalem!For the Lord consoles his people;he protects[NOTE:1] Jerusalem.
notes: Or “redeems.” See the note at 41:14.

verses.zh: 耶和华在万国眼前露出圣臂；地极的人都看见我们　神的救恩了。
verses.en: The Lord reveals[NOTE:1] his royal power[NOTE:2] in the sight of all the nations;the entire[NOTE:3] earth seesour God deliver.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “lays bare”; NLT “will demonstrate.”
Heb “his holy arm.” This is a metonymy for his power.
Heb “the remote regions,” which here stand for the extremities and everything in between.
Heb “the deliverance of our God.” “God” is a subjective genitive here.
verses.commentary:
52:10 Israel was established by YHWH to be a kingdom of priests to the world (cf. Gen. 12:3;
Exod. 19:4-6). However, her covenant unfaithfulness required God's judgment, therefore, the world
never saw God's true character. By God delivering Israel from captivity, first Egypt, then Assyria, and
now Neo-Babylon, all the peoples of the earth will see God's power, love, and blessing.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "has bared His holy arm" The VERB (BDB 362, KB 359, Qal
PERFECT) is anthropomorphic imagery for YHWH getting ready for action/deliverance (cf. Ezek. 4:7).

Often the phrase "with an outstretched arm" denotes the same imagery of Divine actions
(cf. Exod. 6:6; Deut. 4:34; 5:15; 26:8).

▣ "In the sight of all the nations" This is parallel to the next phrase, "all the ends
of the earth may see." This is also parallel to "all flesh will see it" (Isa. 40:5; also note Joel 2:28 for
another universal image).

Isaiah saw clearly YHWH's care and concern for the salvation and inclusion of the
Gentiles (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23; 49:4-5; 51:4-5; 60:1-3; 66:23). Oh, what "good
news" (cf. Eph. 2:11-3:13)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

verses.zh: 你们离开吧！离开吧！从巴比伦出来。不要沾不洁净的物；要从其中出来。你们扛抬耶和华器皿的人哪，务要自洁。
verses.en: Leave! Leave! Get out of there!Don’t touch anything unclean!Get out of it! Stay pure, you who carry the Lord’s holy items.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the vessels of the Lord” (so KJV, NAB).
verses.commentary:
52:11-12 These verses are using God's directions to the priests (cf. Isa. 52:11d; Lev. 22:2) as a way
to assure all covenant people that God is with them and for them (cf. Isa. 52:12). It is a veiled warning
to leave the idolatry of Mesopotamia behind and return to Canaan (i.e. Niphal stem, "purify yourselves,"
cf. Isa. 1:16-17)!

The returnees will take the vessels from YHWH's temple with them (cf. Ezra 1:5-11;
5:14; 6:8; also note 2 Chr. 4 where they are described). They left Neo-Babylon as they had Egypt (cf. Exod. 11:2;
12:35-36) by taking the spoils of the land with them (i.e. imagery of the defeat of the nation and its gods).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible
for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy
Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why was Isaiah using Abraham's call as an encouragement to the Jews in captivity?

- How does creation and the Exodus bring encouragement to exiled Israel and Judah?

- To whom does Isa. 51:16 refer?

- How did God use Israel to reach the Gentiles?

verses.zh: 你们出来必不致急忙，也不致奔逃。因为，耶和华必在你们前头行；以色列的　神必作你们的后盾。
verses.en: Yet do not depart quicklyor leave in a panic.[NOTE:1] For the Lord goes before you;the God of Israel is your rear guard.
notes: Heb “or go in flight”; NAB “leave in headlong flight.”

verses.zh: 我的仆人行事必有智慧（或译：行事通达），必被高举上升，且成为至高。
verses.en: Look, my servant will succeed![NOTE:1] He will be elevated, lifted high, and greatly exalted[NOTE:2]—
notes: Heb “act wisely,” which by metonymy means “succeed.”
This piling up of synonyms emphasizes the degree of the servant’s coming exaltation.

verses.zh: 许多人因他（原文是你）惊奇；他的面貌比别人憔悴；他的形容比世人枯槁。
verses.en: (just as many were horrified by the sight of you)[NOTE:1] he was so disfigured[NOTE:2] he no longer looked like a man;[NOTE:3]his form was so marred he no longer looked human[NOTE:4]—
notes: Some witnesses read “him,” which is more consistent with the context, where the servant is spoken about, not addressed. However, it is possible that the Lord briefly addresses the servant here. The present translation assumes the latter view and places the phrase in parentheses.

Heb “such was the disfigurement.” The noun מִשְׁחַת (mishkhat) occurs only here. It may be derived from the verbal root שָׁחַת (shakhat, “be ruined”; see BDB 1007-8 s.v. שָׁחַת). The construct form appears here before a prepositional phrase (cf. GKC 421 §130.a).
Heb “from a man his appearance.” The preposition מִן (min) here carries the sense “away from,” i.e., “so as not to be.” See BDB 583 s.v.
Heb “and his form from the sons of men.” The preposition מִן (min) here carries the sense “away from,” i.e., “so as not to be.”

verses.zh: 这样，他必洗净（或译：鼓动）许多国民；君王要向他闭口。因所未曾传与他们的，他们必看见；未曾听见的，他们要明白。
verses.en: so now[NOTE:1] he will startle[NOTE:2] many nations.Kings will be shocked by his exaltation,[NOTE:3] for they will witness something unannounced to them,and they will understand something they had not heard about.
notes: This statement completes the sentence begun in v. 14a. The introductory כֵּן (ken) answers to the introductory כַּאֲשֶׁר (kaʾasher) of v. 14a. Verses 14b-15a are parenthetical, explaining why many were horrified.

Traditionally the verb יַזֶּה (yazzeh, a Hiphil stem) has been understood as a causative of נָזָה (nazah, “spurt, spatter”) and translated “sprinkle.” In this case the passage pictures the servant as a priest who “sprinkles” (or spiritually cleanses) the nations. Though the verb נָזָה does occur in the Hiphil with the meaning “sprinkle,” the usual interpretation is problematic. In all other instances where the object or person sprinkled is indicated, the verb is combined with a preposition. This is not the case in Isaiah 52:15, unless one takes the following עָלָיו (ʿalayv, “on him”) with the preceding line. But then one would have to emend the verb to a plural, make the nations the subject of the verb “sprinkle,” and take the servant as the object. Consequently some interpreters doubt the cultic idea of “sprinkling” is present here. Some emend the text; others propose a homonymic root meaning “spring, leap,” which in the Hiphil could mean “cause to leap, startle” and would fit the parallelism of the verse nicely.
Heb “Because of him kings will shut their mouths,” i.e., be speechless.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 52:1-2

1Awake, awake,

Clothe yourself in your strength, O Zion;

Clothe yourself in your beautiful garments,

O Jerusalem, the holy city;

For the uncircumcised and the unclean

Will no longer come into you.

2Shake yourself from the dust, rise up,

O captive Jerusalem;

Loose yourself from the chains around your neck,

O captive daughter of Zion.
